qs.q: A patient is diagnosed with lobar pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. The clinical severity of this infection is largely mediated by a specific surface virulence factor that prevents opsonophagocytosis. What structural component is responsible?
qs.e: The polysaccharide capsule of Streptococcus pneumoniae acts as the primary antiphagocytic virulence factor.

qs.q: An alcoholic patient is hospitalized with severe lobar pneumonia, producing thick, gelatinous, blood-tinged sputum often described as currant jelly. Gram staining reveals encapsulated Gram-negative rods. What virulence factor best explains the characteristic mucoid appearance of the colonies on agar?
o: Proteases secreted that liquefy surrounding host tissue
High levels of lipopolysaccharide O‑antigen chains on the surface
A dense peptidoglycan network cross‑linked throughout the wall
A large polysaccharide capsule that makes colonies sticky
Fimbriae that promote tight intercellular aggregation
qs.e: Klebsiella pneumoniae produces a prominent polysaccharide capsule that gives colonies a characteristically mucoid, sticky texture on agar plates.

qs.q: A patient presents with community-acquired lobar pneumonia. What is the initial stage of inflammatory exudation in the affected lung parenchyma?
qs.e: The initial stage of lobar pneumonia is congestion, characterized by vascular engorgement and intra-alveolar protein-rich fluid.
qs.s: Weekly Year 4: Internal Medicine Exam - October 24, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Lobar pneumonia evolves through four stages. What characterizes the "red hepatization" stage?
o: Enzymatic digestion of exudate with macrophage clearance
Vascular congestion with protein-rich fluid and neutrophils
Alveoli packed with neutrophils, red cells, and fibrin
Lysis of red cells with persistent fibrinosuppurative exudate
qs.e: Red hepatization follows congestion and is characterized by liver-like consistency of the lung. Alveolar spaces are packed with neutrophils, red blood cells, and fibrin — giving the red, firm appearance.

qs.q: Which organism most commonly causes community-acquired lobar pneumonia?
qs.e: Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) causes more than 90% of lobar pneumonias and is the most common cause of community-acquired acute pneumonia overall.

es.q: Identify the most common lung cancer subtype overall and in non-smokers. Additionally, name the most common bacterial pathogen causing lobar pneumonia.
es.m: Adenocarcinoma is the most common lung cancer subtype overall, and also the most common in women and non-smokers. The most common bacterial pathogen causing lobar pneumonia is *Streptococcus pneumoniae*.
